node_definition.done_when: The two writer threads in tests/test_landing_write_races_every_writer.py are coordinated so that a rendezvous that breaks or times out fails the case loudly, naming which thread missed it, instead of being suppressed and letting the writers run unraced. A new case makes the rendezvous break deliberately and asserts that the race case reports failure rather than success. The whole file passes 20 consecutive runs at -n 8 together with tests/test_landing_append_is_commutative.py and tests/test_append_refuses_a_duplicate_id.py, each run in the foreground with its own basetemp. The 20 results are logged, one line per run, in the run directory. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
